summary: One of several fixed texts, picked at run time by an index (a variable or an expression): a phase name, a weekday, a status word such as Rising / Falling, laid out like a plain text.

items.doc: The texts to choose from, e.g. ["Rising", "Falling"]; fixed when the document is built (one text node each)

index.doc: Which item shows, 0-based: a number, a "@variable" or an expression ("weekDay() - 1"). Rounded to the nearest whole number and clamped to the list, so exactly one item always shows

fontSize.doc: Text size in sp (15, the theme's text_md, by default)

textAlign.doc: start, center or end, within the text's own width (matters with fillMaxWidth or several lines)

maxLines.doc: Lines kept at most (unlimited when omitted)

overflow.doc: With maxLines: clip, ellipsis or visible

pitfalls: Use it for a word or phrase from a fixed set chosen at run time (a phase name, a weekday, Rising / Falling, Open / Closed). For a number use textFromFloat; to join a fixed text and a live one use textMerge; for a text the host sends, a text variable

A layout `text` cannot take textSubtext, textTransform or textLookup itself (the Java parser accepts them only among canvas commands), so a name cut out of one string by index needs a canvas command first (see the long-list note); this component needs nothing but layout texts
index is 0-based: weekDay() is 1 (Monday) to 7, so pass "weekDay() - 1"; a fraction of a cycle (a moon phase 0..1) needs "round(@phase * 8) % 8" or similar, not the fraction itself
index is rounded to the nearest whole number and clamped to 0..n-1, so a stray value shows the first or last item, never nothing and never two

It is always expanded, never a definePattern template: a text inside a pattern shares its component id across inflations in shipped Java runtimes (U7). Each call costs about 90 B per item plus its string (Rising / Falling: 174 B; seven weekday names: 713 B)
A literal index works but is pointless (use a plain text); the index is meant to be a variable or an expression that changes

For a long list (more than about 8 items: 31 day numbers, 60 minutes, 12 months on a small budget), cut the name from one padded string instead: a 0-size canvas whose `global` section holds textSubtext (start "(weekDay() - 1) * 9", len 9, varName dayName9) and a textTransform trim (operation 3, varName dayName), then a layout text {"value": "@dayName"}. The global section runs before the layout, so the layout text can read the variable (STR-05 hoists data the same way); seven weekdays cost about 180 B that way, whatever the count. Every name must be padded to the same width

Each item is its own text node; all but one are GONE (visibility 0), so the box takes the size of the one shown and changes size when the choice changes. In a row, neighbours move; give it a fixed width if they shouldn't

The visibility of each item is an INTEGER expression (1 - min(1, abs(k - i)), exact 0 or 1) over the float index k: the player stores a float as its truncated int, so k is rounded first. A float expression that comes out 0.999 would hide every item
Accessibility reads the visible item only (hidden items are GONE), so no label is needed
